::: {#rem-confidence-interval-exact}
#### Why most intervals are conservative

@def-confidence-interval requires the [coverage probability](#def-coverage-probability)
to be at least $1 - \siglevel$ at every $\param$,
which is the same as requiring the [confidence coefficient](#def-confidence-coefficient)
to be at least $1 - \siglevel$.
The coverage probability can depend on $\param$,
and the confidence coefficient is its greatest [lower bound](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/sets.html#def-bound),
which the coverage probability need not attain at any $\param$.
An [exact](#def-exact-confidence-interval) interval has the same coverage probability
at every $\param$.
[Discrete](data.qmd#def-discrete-var) data take only countably many values,
so they usually allow only a [conservative](#def-conservative-confidence-interval) interval,
as @exm-conservative-interval shows.
A [confidence set](#def-confidence-set) drops the requirement that the region be an interval.
:::
